description: Composite figure on strain partitioning in the TD (transverse-direction) sample of a low-density medium-Mn steel, combining EBSD phase + band-contrast (BC) maps with EBSD-derived shear-strain maps and two line profiles. (a1) is the phase + BC map of the entire probed area (100 µm scale bar, TD marked) with a red rectangle labelled "UFG"; (a2)-(a5) are its shear-strain maps at engineering strains 5%, 10%, 15% and 20%, the 20% map carrying boxes "1" and "2". (b1) is the phase + BC map of the UFG γ+α region (5 µm scale bar) with (b2)-(b5) its strain maps; (c1) and (d1) are the isolated FCC (γ) and BCC (α/δ) phase maps of the area in (b1), with (c2)-(c5) and (d2)-(d5) the matching single-phase strain maps. (e1) and (e2) plot shear strain (%) versus distance (µm) along the arrows marked in the inset strain maps, with δ and γ+α regions labelled and red dashed lines marking δ/γ+α band boundaries. A shared colour bar gives shear strain 0-30%; legend: FCC cyan, BCC grey; loading-direction arrow at bottom. Strain rises with engineering strain and localises in δ-ferrite in (e2), while the UFG γ+α region stays low; black arrows in (d5) mark phase-boundary strain concentration.

observations.observation: Panel (a1) is an EBSD phase + BC map of the whole probed area of the TD sample with a 100 µm scale bar and TD marked; cyan regions are FCC and grey regions BCC, arranged in bands along the map.
A red rectangular frame labelled 'UFG' in (a1) identifies the sub-region re-imaged at higher magnification in (b1) with a 5 µm scale bar.
The strain maps (a2)-(a5), (b2)-(b5), (c2)-(c5) and (d2)-(d5) are each labelled with their engineering strain (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%) in a white box in the upper-left corner.

A single colour bar at the bottom of the figure maps shear strain from 0 to 30% (ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30), with dark blue for low and red for high strain; the legend colours are FCC = cyan and BCC = grey, and a double-headed arrow marks the loading direction.

In profile (e2) the two δ regions at the left (x ≈ 1-2 µm) and right (x ≈ 17-22 µm) edges, delimited by red dashed vertical lines, show shear strain between the 20% and 25% gridlines, whereas the intervening region labelled 'γ+α' is mostly between 5% and 17%.
In profile (e1) the δ region at the left edge reaches values close to the 30% axis limit, while the γ+α region to the right fluctuates around 15-20%.
Black arrows in panel (d5) (20% engineering strain) mark locations of localised high shear strain along BCC phase boundaries / interphase boundaries.
The inset strain maps in (e1) and (e2) show the arrow (white) along which the line profiles were taken, with a scale bar and a numeric label ('1' in e1, '2' in e2) matching the white boxes in (a5).
The caption states that (a1-a5), (b1-b5), (c1-c5) and (d1-d5) show the shear strain distribution of the areas in (a), (b), (c) and (d) respectively, at engineering strains from 5% to 20%.
The caption states that (e) shows local strain across different representative phase regions along the arrow marked in the inset strain maps.
The citing text asserts that the TD sample shows more pronounced strain heterogeneity, already visible at low magnification in Fig. 11(a).
The citing text states that the higher strain is concentrated in the δ-phase in the TD sample (Fig. 11(e)), a phenomenon not observed in the RD sample.
The citing text states that Figs. 11(c) and (d) reveal a relatively higher strain inside the γ-α' mixed phase than in the α-ferrite region.

The citing text states that above 15% plastic deformation, strain concentration near the phase boundaries is observed (arrows in Fig. 11(d)), attributed to strain incompatibility between austenite and ferrite increasing the number of GNDs at phase boundaries.
The citing text states that the average strain of δ-ferrite in the TD sample is about 1.26 times higher than that of the γ+α aggregates (Fig. 12(b)), consistent with Figs. 10 and 11.

subfigures.description: EBSD phase + BC map of the entire probed area of the TD sample, 100 µm scale bar, TD direction marked; a red rectangular frame labelled 'UFG' marks the sub-region analysed in (b)-(d). Cyan/teal phase (FCC) and grey phase (BCC) appear as banded regions.

Shear-strain maps of the area in (a1) at engineering strains 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% (each labelled in a white box, 100 µm scale bar). Strain increases progressively with engineering strain; the 20% map contains white boxes labelled '1' and '2' whose line profiles are plotted in (e1)/(e2).
EBSD phase + BC map of the UFG γ+α region (red frame in (a1)), 5 µm scale bar, showing fine equiaxed γ grains and elongated α/δ regions.
Shear-strain maps of the UFG γ+α region at 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% engineering strain, 5 µm scale bar; strain becomes progressively more heterogeneous with increasing deformation.
Isolated FCC (γ) phase map of the area in (b1), 5 µm scale bar, with the FCC phase highlighted and the BCC phase masked out.
Shear-strain maps for the FCC phase only at 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% engineering strain, 5 µm scale bar; the masked (non-FCC) regions remain white.
Isolated BCC (α/δ) phase map of the area in (b1), 5 µm scale bar, BCC phase shown in grey.
Shear-strain maps for the BCC phase only at 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% engineering strain, 5 µm scale bar; in (d5) black arrows point to sites of strain concentration along BCC/BCC or phase boundaries.

Line profile of shear strain (%) versus distance (µm) over roughly 0-11 µm across the region marked '1' in (a5), following the arrow in the inset strain map; the δ region at the left edge reaches the highest values near the 30% axis limit while the γ+α region sits around 15-20% with strong point-to-point scatter.

Line profile of shear strain (%) versus distance (µm) over roughly 0-22 µm across the region marked '2' in (a5); two δ regions at the left (x ≈ 1-2 µm) and right (x ≈ 17-22 µm) edges, delimited by red dashed vertical lines, show strain between the 20% and 25% gridlines, while the intervening γ+α region (labelled 'γ+α') shows values mostly between 5% and 17%, with a minimum of about 5% immediately before the right δ band.
